final.memo:
FANUC Corporation is a world-class manufacturer of factory automation controls and robots that is currently marred by a massive, unproductive cash-hoarding balance sheet [D01], [D02]. While the company maintains an industry-leading 36.4% operating margin, it remains mispriced by a market that treats it as a standard cyclical machinery play [D05], [D06].

Our sum-of-the-parts analysis values the core business at approximately ¥3,700bn, which, when combined with the company’s ¥928bn in cash and securities, supports a intrinsic value of ¥26,200 per share [D02], [D04]. Compared to peers like Yaskawa, which operates at significantly lower margins, FANUC’s current P/E of 22.2x fails to reflect the potential for a capital-efficiency re-rate [D04], [D06].

The market’s focus on cyclical risks in automotive and smartphone capex obscures the reality that FANUC’s cash pile is essentially doing nothing for shareholders [D02], [D05]. We believe that by engaging with the board to initiate a rigorous capital return policy—including share repurchases and elevated dividends—the company can unlock substantial trapped value [D03].

Our plan is to initiate direct, private engagement with the board to demand these reforms over the next two quarters [D03]. We expect management to pivot toward global governance standards; if this polite, constructive approach is ignored, we are prepared to escalate our activities [D03]. We have established a high-conviction position with a 5% target NAV allocation, using common shares as our primary instrument, while hedging market beta via Nikkei 225 index puts [D04], [D05].
